stem: When did Bal Gangadhar Tilak get the title Lokmanya?
expl: In June 1897 A.D., the Chapekar brothers attacked Rand, the president of the Plague Committee of Poona and killed Lieutenant Ayerst. It was alleged that the Brahmins of Poona, under the leadership of Tilak, had conspired in the murder of Rand and Ayerst. In July 1897 A.D., Tilak was arrested on charges of sedition under section 124-A of the Indian Penal Code for inciting murder through his writings. He was prosecuted and sentenced to 18 months imprisonment, which caused huge protests across the country. For this reason Tilak became popular as an all India leader and the public gave him the title of 'Lokmanya'.

stem: When did the attempt of murder of Kingsford was made at Muzaffarpur ?

On the evening of April 30, 1908 A.D., the duo waited in front of the gate of European club for the carriage of Kingsford to arrive. When a vehicle came out of the gate, they threw bombs and blew up the carriage. Unfortunately, the vehicle was not carrying Kingsford and instead, two innocent British ladies- Mrs. and Miss Kennedy (the wife and daughter of barrister Pringle Kennedy) were killed. The revolutionary duo fl ed. Prafulla committed suicide and Khudiram was later arrested and hanged.

stem: Muzaffar Ahmad, S.A. Dange, Shaukat Usmani and Nalini Gupta were jailed for which conspiracy?
expl: When Socialist ideology spread in India during the third decade of 20th century, the Government took steps for suppression. Socialist leaders were put in Jail. Shripad Amrit Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, Shaukat Usmani and Nalini Gupta were put into jail on false accusations of involvement in Kanpur Bol Shevik conspiracy case. All were sentenced to four years imprisonment.

stem: Who among the following organized the famous Chittagong armoury raid?
expl: Chittagong armoury raid was an attempt to raid the armoury of the police and auxiliary forces at Chittagong in Bengal. It was organised by Surya Sen who was also famous by the name of ‘’Master Da’’ The Indian Republican Army (IRA) was established by Surya Sen in Bengal and on 18th April, 1930 A.D., the plan was put into implementation by the members of IRA namely Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath, Nirmal Sen, Ambika Chakrobarty, Naresh Roy, Kalpana Dutt, Anand Gupta, Tegrabal etc. including Surya Sen. Struggle took place on 22nd April, 1930 A.D. between members of Government forces and members of IRA in which 80 soldiers and 12 revolutionaries were killed. On 16 February, 1933 A.D., Surya Sen was arrested and put through legal proceedings and ultimately hanged on 12th January, 1934 A.D.

stem: Martyr of least age in the war of Independence was – (a) Sukhdev (b) Ashfaqullah Khan
expl: (1) Sukhdev- Birth - 15 May, 1907, Hanged- 23 March 1931 Age when hanged was 23 years, 10 months, 8 days (2) Ashfaq Ullah Khan- Birth 22 October,1900, Hanged, 19 December 1927 Age when hanged was 27 years, 1 months, 28 days (3) Khudiram Bose- Birth 3 December, 1889 Hanged- 11 August, 1908 Age when hanged was 18 years, 8 months 8 days (4) Hemu Kalani - Birth 23 March 1923 Hanged- 21 January 1943 Age when hanged was 19 years, 9 months, 29 days So, it is manifest from the above that in the given options during the struggle for Independence, Khudiram Bose was hanged at least age, so option (c) is the correct answer.

stem: On what charge was Jatin Das arrested:
expl: Jatindra (or Jatin) participated in Gandhi’s Non-Cooperation Movement in 1921 A.D. Later on, he came in contact with revolutionaries and participated in bomb-making to help Bhagat Singh and comrades. On 14th June, 1929 A.D. he was arrested on such type of charges under the supplementary Lahore Conspiracy Case. He started a hunger strike for Jail reforms, and due to this long hunger strike which lasted 63 days, Jatin died on 13th September, 1929 A.D.

stem: Under whose chairmanship a committee was formed to defend the accused in Kakori Case?
expl: Yogesh Chandra Chatterjee was one of the founder members of Hindustan Republican Association. He was sentenced to life imprisonment in Kakori Case (Kakori train action). He wrote in his book ‘In search of Freedom’ that Pandit Motilal Nehru under Leadership of Govind Ballabh Pant formed the Kakori Case (Kakori train action day) Defense Committee. In an article by Shankar Narayan Rao at PIB website, it is mentioned that in this case President of the defence committee was Pandit Motilal Nehru. We at this moment considering Shri Chatterjee's book as a primary source consider option (b) as the correct answer. Initially, UPPSC has considered option (d) as the correct option, but later on in its revised answer sheet it supports option (b) as the correct answer.

stem: Who among the following was NOT an early member of the 'Naujawan-Sabha' formed in 1926 A.D.?
expl: Naujawan Bharat Sabha was a left-wing Indian association that sought to foment revolution against the British Raj by gathering together worker and peasant youths by disseminating Marxist idea. It was founded by Bhagat Singh in March 1926 A.D. along with Chhabil Das, Yaspal, Ramchandra, Bhagvati Charan Vohra etc. It was part of the Hindustan Republican Association. Ambika Chakravarti was a member of Chittagong Jugantar Party. He took part in the Chittagong Armoury Raid led by Surya Sen. He joined the Naujawan Bharat Sabha at later stage.

stem: Which of the following revolutionary was hanged in the Gorakhpur Jail-
expl: Kakori event happened on 9th August 1925 A.D. In this event, 43 revolutionaries were arrested. Among these freedom fi ghters Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaq Ullah Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri, etc. were maliciously prosecuted and death sentence were awarded to them. Ram Prasad Bismil was hanged in Gorakhpur Jail, Rajendra Lahiri was hanged in Gonda and Roshan Singh in Allahabad (now Prayagraj) and Ashfaq Ullah was hanged in Faizabad (now Ayodhya).
